findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error
findings.failure_mode: Corrupted, missing, or unreadable file aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a side-effect I/O call inside data-processing logic
findings.failure_mode: Breaks functional-core purity; logs leak into downstream consumers and cannot be suppressed in tests without global state mutation
findings.fix: Remove println! from the core pipeline; move any logging to the imperative shell boundary

findings.failure_mode: Empty line or malformed row with no comma panics via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on the (name, rest) tuple

findings.failure_mode: Row with only one comma-separated field panics via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match on the (name, rest) tuple

findings.failure_mode: Malformed value field aborts the entire load instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Return Result<Record, ParseError> and propagate parse failure with ? or map_err

findings.problem: Lossy cast as u16 truncates values outside u16 range silently
findings.failure_mode: A value like 50000 becomes 44160 without any error or warning, producing silently incorrect data
findings.fix: Use u32::try_from or check range with value <= u16::MAX before converting

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates all parts into a Vec<String> when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation per line; split_once(',') would avoid the Vec entirely
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to extract name and value parts without collecting all fields

findings.problem: load_orders performs I/O (fs::read_to_string) and parsing in the same function that builds domain data
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic in isolation from filesystem; pure core is not separated from imperative shell
findings.fix: Split into a pure parse_record(&str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> and a shell function load_orders(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> that calls read_to_string then maps parse_record

findings.problem: Record has pub fields with String name and u16 value; no domain invariants enforced by the type
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct Record with empty names or negative/overflow values outside the parser
findings.fix: Make fields private and provide a constructor or parse method that validates invariants; use newtype for name (e.g., RecordName(String)) if domain rules exist

findings.problem: load_orders returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures are expressed via panic
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish I/O errors from parse errors or handle them programmatically
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, Box<dyn Error>> or a domain-specific error enum with I/O and parse variants

findings.problem: part.trim().to_string() allocates a new String for every field even though only parts[0] and parts[1] are consumed
findings.failure_mode: Redundant heap allocation per line; &str slices from split_once would avoid this
findings.fix: Keep trimmed &str references from split_once until the final Record construction

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure load_orders throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data for per-line allocation count or total heap usage
no allocation audit showing try_reserve usage or capacity planning
no command-level evidence that load_orders handles edge cases (empty file, single line, malformed rows)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. All failures are expressed through panic rather than typed errors. The entire function is a single monolithic I/O-and-parsing unit that cannot be unit-tested in isolation. Any file content can crash the process. Truncation silently corrupts data. Without benchmarks there is no evidence for allocation or throughput claims.
